summary: Yuko Kamishima is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. She studied at the University of Tokyo, including as a research student under Ekai Kawaguchi, and held a post at Ritsumeikan University.

Yuko Matsuda is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who studied at Aoyama Gakuin Women's Junior College. She held a post at Kyushu Ryukoku Junior College (attested 2001) and taught Catherine Ludvik.

Yuko Yokochi is an Indologist who earned an MA at the University of Tokyo under Minoru Hara and Katsuhiko Kamimura, and a PhD from the University of Groningen (by 2004). At Kyoto University, she was Associate Professor (attested 2002) and Professor (attested 2012–2021).

Sinologist Yukteshwar Kumar studied at Visva-Bharati University, Peking University, and Jawaharlal Nehru University (~1993–2003) under Tan Chung. He held posts at Jawaharlal Nehru University, the University of Delhi, and the University of Bath (~2012).
Yulian Zeng is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a Master of Arts at Fo Guang University under the supervision of Kirill Jurievitch Solonin (attested 2010).
Yumi Katayama specializes in Indology, philosophy, and Buddhist studies. She was a PhD student at Hiroshima University (attested 2007) and studied under supervisor Kenyu Mitomo (attested 2013).
Yumi Nakamoto works in Buddhist studies and history and archaeology. She studied at Ryukoku University (attested 2014) and held posts there as a公募研究員 in 2012 and as a大学院研究生 (attested 2014).
Yumiko Ishihama is a scholar of Tibetology, history and archaeology, and Buddhist studies. She studied at Waseda University (~1980–1989) and held a post there around 1997.

Yun Ji is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Sinology who completed a PhD in Chinese literature at Fudan University by 2006. He held an assistant professor post at the Buddhist College of Singapore (attested 2015).

Yun-hua Jan was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Sinology, and religious studies who studied under Yun-shan Tan. He was a Research Fellow at Visva-Bharati University (1953) and a Professor at McMaster University (attested 1984–1990).

Yun-shan Tan worked in Sinology, Buddhist studies, and Indology. Educated at Wenjiang Shuyuan, Mijiang Academy, Chuanshan Academy, and Hunan Normal University, he studied under several mentors including Taixu, taught at Lida Academy, and served as Professor of Chinese Studies at Visva-Bharati University.
Yungfen Ma is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Sinology who earned a PhD at Columbia University under the doctoral supervision of Chun-fang Yu (attested 2011).
Yusen Kashiwahara was a scholar of Buddhist studies and history and archaeology. He studied at Otani University and served there as a professor (~1957–1987).

Yusho Miyasaka was an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Tohoku University (~1945–1948). He held posts at Koyasan University (助教授 ~1955–1974), Shuchiin University, and Nagoya University (Professor Emeritus in 1976).

Yusho Wakahara is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who studied at Ryukoku University under Eshō Mikogami. He held posts at Hanazono University (lecturer, attested 1987) and Ryukoku University (助教授, attested 1987–1999; 教授, attested 2011–2013).
Yutai Ikeda was a Buddhist studies scholar who held posts at Otani University and Doho University, where he was Emeritus Professor (attested 2006).

Yutaka Hirata specialized in history, archaeology, Buddhist studies, and Japanology. He studied at Kyushu University (~1950–1954), later becoming Professor Emeritus there (~1995–2013), and also held a post at Nagasaki Junshin Catholic University.

Yutaka Iwamoto was an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Kyoto University (~1931–1934), supervised by Toru Haneda and Hidenaka Tanaka. He held academic posts at Kyoto Tachibana University (~1977–1982) and Soka University (~1982–1988).
Yutaka Kawasaki is a scholar of Indology and Buddhist studies who studied under Seio Okuda. He held a post at the University of Tokyo (attested 2024).

Indologist and linguist Yutaka Ochihara studied at Kyoto University (~1944–1947) and the University of Pennsylvania (1951–1954). He was an Associate Professor (1957) and Professor (1972–1986) at Kyoto University, and a Professeur étranger at Collège de France (1985).
